Slots.name: specimen_collector_sample_id
Slots.title: specimen collector sample ID
Slots.description: The user-defined name for the sample.
Slots.comments: Store the collector sample ID. If this number is considered identifiable information, provide an alternative ID. Be sure to store the key that maps between the original and alternative IDs for traceability and follow up if necessary. Every collector sample ID from a single submitter must be unique. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_service_provider_name
Slots.title: third party lab service provider name
Slots.description: The name of the third party company or laboratory that provided services.
Slots.comments: Provide the full, unabbreviated name of the company or laboratory.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_sample_id
Slots.title: third party lab sample ID
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sample by a third party service provider.
Slots.comments: Store the sample identifier supplied by the third party services provider.

Slots.name: case_id
Slots.title: case ID
Slots.description: The identifier used to specify an epidemiologically detected case of disease.
Slots.comments: Provide the case identifer. The case ID greatly facilitates linkage between laboratory and epidemiological data. The case ID may be considered identifiable information. Consult the data steward before sharing.

Slots.name: related_specimen_primary_id
Slots.title: Related specimen primary ID
Slots.description: The primary ID of a related specimen previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Store the primary ID of the related specimen previously submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory so that the samples can be linked and tracked through the system.

Slots.name: irida_sample_name
Slots.title: IRIDA sample name
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sequenced isolate in IRIDA.
Slots.comments: Store the IRIDA sample name. The IRIDA sample name will be created by the individual entering data into the IRIDA platform. IRIDA samples may be linked to metadata and sequence data, or just metadata alone. It is recommended that the IRIDA sample name be the same as, or contain, the specimen collector sample ID for better traceability. It is also recommended that the IRIDA sample name mirror the GISAID accession. IRIDA sample names cannot contain slashes. Slashes should be replaced by underscores. See IRIDA documentation for more information regarding special characters (https://irida.corefacility.ca/documentation/user/user/samples/#adding-a-new-sample).

Slots.name: umbrella_bioproject_accession
Slots.title: umbrella bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number assigned to the umbrella BioProject.
Slots.comments: Store the umbrella BioProject accession by selecting it from the picklist in the template. The umbrella BioProject accession will be identical for all CanCOGen submitters. Different provinces will have their own BioProjects, however these BioProjects will be linked under one umbrella BioProject.

Slots.name: bioproject_accession
Slots.title: bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number of the BioProject(s) to which the BioSample belongs.
Slots.comments: Store the BioProject accession number. BioProjects are an organizing tool that links together raw sequence data, assemblies, and their associated metadata. Each province will be assigned a different bioproject accession number by the National Microbiology Lab. A valid NCBI BioProject accession has prefix PRJN e.g., PRJNA12345, and is created once at the beginning of a new sequencing project.

Slots.name: biosample_accession
Slots.title: biosample accession
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a BioSample in INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the BioSample submission. NCBI BioSamples will have the prefix SAMN.

Slots.name: sra_accession
Slots.title: SRA accession
Slots.description: The Sequence Read Archive (SRA) identifier linking raw read data, methodological metadata and quality control metrics submitted to the INSDC.
Slots.comments: Store the accession assigned to the submitted "run". NCBI-SRA accessions start with SRR.

Slots.name: genbank_accession
Slots.title: GenBank accession
Slots.description: The GenBank identifier assigned to the sequence in the INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from a GenBank submission (viral genome assembly).

Slots.name: gisaid_accession
Slots.title: GISAID accession
Slots.description: The GISAID accession number assigned to the sequence.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the GISAID submission.

Slots.name: gisaid_virus_name
Slots.title: GISAID virus name
Slots.description: The user-defined name of the virus, specified in the organism-specific format prescribed by the GISAID database.
Slots.comments: Provide the GISAID virus name, which should be written in the format: A/Province/Country/SampleID/year

Slots.name: sample_collected_by
Slots.title: sample collected by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that collected the original sample.
Slots.comments: The name of the sample collector should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions e.g. Public Health Agency of Canada, Public Health Ontario, BC Centre for Disease Control. The sample collector specified is at the discretion of the data provider (i.e. may be hospital, provincial public health lab, or other).

Slots.name: sample_collector_contact_email
Slots.title: sample collector contact email
Slots.description: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sample.
Slots.comments: The email address can represent a specific individual or lab e.g. johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca

Slots.name: sequenced_by
Slots.title: sequenced by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that generated the sequence.
Slots.comments: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multiple submissions. If submitting specimens rather than sequencing data, please put the "National Microbiology Laboratory (NML)".

Slots.name: sequence_submitted_by
Slots.title: sequence submitted by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that generated the sequence.
Slots.comments: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions. If submitting specimens rather than sequencing data, please put the "National Microbiology Laboratory (NML)".

Slots.name: sample_collection_date
Slots.title: sample collection date
Slots.description: The date on which the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Sample collection date is critical for surveillance and many types of analyses. Required granularity includes year, month and day. If this date is considered identifiable information, it is acceptable to add "jitter" by adding or subtracting a calendar day (acceptable by GISAID). Alternatively, ”received date” may be used as a substitute. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: sample_collection_date_precision
Slots.title: sample collection date precision
Slots.description: The precision to which the "sample collection date" was provided.
Slots.comments: Provide the precision of granularity to the "day", "month", or "year" for the date provided in the "sample collection date" field. The "sample collection date" will be truncated to the precision specified upon export; "day" for "YYYY-MM-DD", "month" for "YYYY-MM", or "year" for "YYYY".

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_country
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (country)
Slots.description: The country where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the country name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_state_province_territory
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (state/province/territory)
Slots.description: The province/territory where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the province/territory name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: organism
Slots.title: organism
Slots.description: Taxonomic name of the organism.
Slots.comments: Select the type of influenza virus from the picklist provided.

Slots.name: isolate
Slots.title: isolate
Slots.description: Identifier of the specific isolate.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling
Slots.title: purpose of sampling
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: The reason a sample was collected may provide information about potential biases in sampling strategy. Provide the purpose of sampling from the picklist in the template. Most likely, the sample was collected for diagnostic testing. The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing, which should be indicated in the "purpose of sequencing" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling_details
Slots.title: purpose of sampling details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was collected, providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was collected using free text. The description may include the importance of the sample for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. If details are not available, provide a null value.
Slots.examples: The sample was collected to investigate the prevalence of variants associated with mink-to-human transmission in Canada.

Slots.name: nml_submitted_specimen_type
Slots.title: NML submitted specimen type
Slots.description: The type of specimen submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory (NML) for testing.
Slots.comments: This information is required for upload through the CNPHI LaSER system. Select the specimen type from the pick list provided. If sequence data is being submitted rather than a specimen for testing, select “Not Applicable”.

Slots.name: related_specimen_relationship_type
Slots.title: Related specimen relationship type
Slots.description: The relationship of the current specimen to the specimen/sample previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Provide the tag that describes how the previous sample is related to the current sample being submitted from the pick list provided, so that the samples can be linked and tracked in the system.

Slots.name: presampling_activity
Slots.title: presampling_activity
Slots.description: The upstream activities or variables that may affect the sample collected.
Slots.comments: If there was an activity that would affect the sample prior to collection (this is different than sample processing), provide the activities by selecting one or more values from the template pick list. If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Slots.name: presampling_activity_details
Slots.title: presampling activity details
Slots.description: The details of the activities or variables that may affect the sample collected.
Slots.comments: Briefly describe the presampling details using free text.
Slots.examples: Patient was previously infected. Sample taken during convalescence.

Slots.name: anatomical_material
Slots.title: anatomical material
Slots.description: A substance obtained from an anatomical part of an organism e.g. tissue, blood.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical material was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: anatomical_part
Slots.title: anatomical part
Slots.description: An anatomical part of an organism e.g. oropharynx.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical part was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: body_product
Slots.title: body product
Slots.description: A substance excreted/secreted from an organism e.g. feces, urine, sweat.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a body product was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_device
Slots.title: collection device
Slots.description: The instrument or container used to collect the sample e.g. swab.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a device was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_method
Slots.title: collection method
Slots.description: The process used to collect the sample e.g. phlebotomy, necropsy.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a collection method was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_protocol
Slots.title: collection protocol
Slots.description: The name and version of a particular protocol used for sampling.
Slots.comments: Free text.

Slots.name: specimen_processing
Slots.title: specimen processing
Slots.description: Any processing applied to the sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Critical for interpreting data. Select all the applicable processes from the pick list. If virus was passaged, include information in "lab host", "passage number", and "passage method" fields. If none of the processes in the pick list apply, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: specimen_processing_details
Slots.title: specimen processing details
Slots.description: Detailed information regarding the processing applied to a sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of any processing details applied to a sample.
Slots.examples: 25 swabs were pooled and further prepared as a single sample during library prep.

Slots.name: biomaterial_extracted
Slots.title: biomaterial extracted
Slots.description: The biomaterial extracted from samples for the purpose of sequencing.
Slots.comments: Provide the biomaterial extracted from the picklist in the template.

Slots.name: host_common_name
Slots.title: host (common name)
Slots.description: The commonly used name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Common name e.g. human, bat. If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable.

Slots.name: host_scientific_name
Slots.title: host (scientific name)
Slots.description: The taxonomic, or scientific name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Scientific name e.g. Homo sapiens, If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable

Slots.name: host_health_state
Slots.title: host health state
Slots.description: Health status of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_status_details
Slots.title: host health status details
Slots.description: Further details pertaining to the health or disease status of the host at time of collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_outcome
Slots.title: host health outcome
Slots.description: Disease outcome in the host.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_disease
Slots.title: host disease
Slots.description: The name of the disease experienced by the host.
Slots.comments: Select "Influenza" from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_age
Slots.title: host age
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling.
Slots.comments: Enter the age of the host in years. If not available, provide a null value. If there is not host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_age_unit
Slots.title: host age unit
Slots.description: The unit used to measure the host age, in either months or years.
Slots.comments: Indicate whether the host age is in months or years. Age indicated in months will be binned to the 0 - 9 year age bin.

Slots.name: host_age_bin
Slots.title: host age bin
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling, expressed as an age group.
Slots.comments: Select the corresponding host age bin from the pick list provided in the template. If not available, provide a null value.

Slots.name: host_gender
Slots.title: host gender
Slots.description: The gender of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: Select the corresponding host gender from the pick list provided in the template. If not available, provide a null value. If there is no host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_subject_id
Slots.title: host subject ID
Slots.description: A unique identifier by which each host can be referred to e.g. #131
Slots.comments: Provide the host identifier. Should be a unique, user-defined identifier.

Slots.name: host_vaccination_status
Slots.title: host vaccination status
Slots.description: The vaccination status of the host (fully vaccinated, partially vaccinated, or not vaccinated).
Slots.comments: Select the vaccination status of the host from the pick list.

Slots.name: vaccination_history
Slots.title: vaccination history
Slots.description: A description of the vaccines received and the administration dates of a series of vaccinations against a specific disease or a set of diseases.
Slots.comments: Free text description of the dates and vaccines administered against a particular disease/set of diseases. It is also acceptable to concatenate the individual dose information (vaccine name, vaccination date) separated by semicolons.

Slots.name: exposure_event
Slots.title: exposure event
Slots.description: Event leading to exposure.
Slots.comments: Select an exposure event from the pick list provided in the template. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_contact_level
Slots.title: exposure contact level
Slots.description: The exposure transmission contact type.
Slots.comments: Select direct or indirect exposure from the pick-list.

Slots.name: host_role
Slots.title: host role
Slots.description: The role of the host in relation to the exposure setting.
Slots.comments: Select the host's personal role(s) from the pick list provided in the template. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_setting
Slots.title: exposure setting
Slots.description: The setting leading to exposure.
Slots.comments: Select the host exposure setting(s) from the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_details
Slots.title: exposure details
Slots.description: Additional host exposure information.
Slots.comments: Free text description of the exposure.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sequencing
Slots.title: purpose of sequencing
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was sequenced.
Slots.comments: The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing. The reason a sample was sequenced may provide information about potential biases in sequencing strategy. Provide the purpose of sequencing from the picklist in the template. The reason for sample collection should be indicated in the "purpose of sampling" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sequencing_details
Slots.title: purpose of sequencing details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was sequenced providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was sequenced using free text. The description may include the importance of the sequences for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. Suggested standardized descriotions include: Screened for S gene target failure (S dropout), Screened for mink variants, Screened for B.1.1.7 variant, Screened for B.1.135 variant, Screened for P.1 variant, Screened due to travel history, Screened due to close contact with infected individual, Assessing public health control measures, Determining early introductions and spread, Investigating airline-related exposures, Investigating temporary foreign worker, Investigating remote regions, Investigating health care workers, Investigating schools/universities, Investigating reinfection.

Slots.name: sequencing_date
Slots.title: sequencing date
Slots.description: The date the sample was sequenced.
Slots.comments: ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: amplicon_size
Slots.title: amplicon size
Slots.description: The length of the amplicon generated by PCR amplification.
Slots.comments: Provide the amplicon size, including the units.

Slots.name: library_preparation_kit
Slots.title: library preparation kit
Slots.description: The name of the DNA library preparation kit used to generate the library being sequenced.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the library preparation kit used.

Slots.name: sequencing_instrument
Slots.title: sequencing instrument
Slots.description: The model of the sequencing instrument used.
Slots.comments: Select a sequencing instrument from the picklist provided in the template.

Slots.name: sequencing_protocol
Slots.title: sequencing protocol
Slots.description: The protocol used to generate the sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of the methods and materials used to generate the sequence. Suggested text, fill in information where indicated.: "Viral sequencing was performed following a tiling amplicon strategy using the <fill in> primer scheme. Sequencing was performed using a <fill in> sequencing instrument. Libraries were prepared using <fill in> library kit. "
Slots.examples: Genomes were generated through amplicon sequencing of 300 bp amplicons with ARTIC schema primers. Libraries were created using Illumina DNA Prep kits, and sequence data was produced using Miseq Micro v2 (500 cycles) sequencing kits.

Slots.name: amplicon_pcr_primer_scheme
Slots.title: amplicon pcr primer scheme
Slots.description: The specifications of the primers (primer sequences, binding positions, fragment size generated etc) used to generate the amplicons to be sequenced.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version of the primer scheme used to generate the amplicons for sequencing.

Slots.name: raw_sequence_data_processing_method
Slots.title: raw sequence data processing method
Slots.description: The names of the software and version number used for raw data processing such as removing barcodes, adapter trimming, filtering etc.
Slots.comments: Provide the software name followed by the version e.g. Trimmomatic v. 0.38, Porechop v. 0.2.3

Slots.name: dehosting_method
Slots.title: dehosting method
Slots.description: The method used to remove host reads from the pathogen sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version number of the software used to remove host reads.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_software_name
Slots.title: consensus sequence software name
Slots.description: The name of software used to generate the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_software_version
Slots.title: consensus sequence software version
Slots.description: The version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: breadth_of_coverage_value
Slots.title: breadth of coverage value
Slots.description: The percentage of the reference genome covered by the sequenced data, to a prescribed depth.
Slots.comments: Provide value as a percent.

Slots.name: depth_of_coverage_value
Slots.title: depth of coverage value
Slots.description: The average number of reads representing a given nucleotide in the reconstructed sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide value as a fold of coverage.

Slots.name: depth_of_coverage_threshold
Slots.title: depth of coverage threshold
Slots.description: The threshold used as a cut-off for the depth of coverage.
Slots.comments: Provide the threshold fold coverage.

Slots.name: number_of_base_pairs_sequenced
Slots.title: number of base pairs sequenced
Slots.description: The number of total base pairs generated by the sequencing process.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: consensus_genome_length
Slots.title: consensus genome length
Slots.description: Size of the reconstructed genome described as the number of base pairs.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: reference_genome_accession
Slots.title: reference genome accession
Slots.description: A persistent, unique identifier of a genome database entry.
Slots.comments: Provide the accession number of the reference genome.

Slots.name: bioinformatics_protocol
Slots.title: bioinformatics protocol
Slots.description: A description of the overall bioinformatics strategy used.
Slots.comments: Further details regarding the methods used to process raw data, and/or generate assemblies, and/or generate consensus sequences can. This information can be provided in an SOP or protocol or pipeline/workflow. Provide the name and version number of the protocol, or a GitHub link to a pipeline or workflow.

Slots.name: gene_name_1
Slots.title: gene name 1
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of the gene used in the test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_1
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 1
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: gene_name_2
Slots.title: gene name 2
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of another gene used in an RT-PCR test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_2
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 2
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the second diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: gene_name_3
Slots.title: gene name 3
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of another gene used in an RT-PCR test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_3
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 3
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the second diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: authors
Slots.title: authors
Slots.description: Names of individuals contributing to the processes of sample collection, sequence generation, analysis, and data submission.
Slots.comments: Include the first and last names of all individuals that should be attributed, separated by a comma.
Slots.examples: Tejinder Singh, Fei Hu, Joe Blogs

Slots.name: dataharmonizer_provenance
Slots.title: DataHarmonizer provenance
Slots.description: The DataHarmonizer software and template version provenance.
Slots.comments: The current software and template version information will be automatically generated in this field after the user utilizes the "validate" function. This information will be generated regardless as to whether the row is valid of not.

Slots.name: specimen_collector_sample_id
Slots.title: specimen collector sample ID
Slots.description: The user-defined name for the sample.
Slots.comments: Store the collector sample ID. If this number is considered identifiable information, provide an alternative ID. Be sure to store the key that maps between the original and alternative IDs for traceability and follow up if necessary. Every collector sample ID from a single submitter must be unique. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_service_provider_name
Slots.title: third party lab service provider name
Slots.description: The name of the third party company or laboratory that provided services.
Slots.comments: Provide the full, unabbreviated name of the company or laboratory.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_sample_id
Slots.title: third party lab sample ID
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sample by a third party service provider.
Slots.comments: Store the sample identifier supplied by the third party services provider.

Slots.name: case_id
Slots.title: case ID
Slots.description: The identifier used to specify an epidemiologically detected case of disease.
Slots.comments: Provide the case identifer. The case ID greatly facilitates linkage between laboratory and epidemiological data. The case ID may be considered identifiable information. Consult the data steward before sharing.

Slots.name: related_specimen_primary_id
Slots.title: Related specimen primary ID
Slots.description: The primary ID of a related specimen previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Store the primary ID of the related specimen previously submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory so that the samples can be linked and tracked through the system.

Slots.name: irida_sample_name
Slots.title: IRIDA sample name
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sequenced isolate in IRIDA.
Slots.comments: Store the IRIDA sample name. The IRIDA sample name will be created by the individual entering data into the IRIDA platform. IRIDA samples may be linked to metadata and sequence data, or just metadata alone. It is recommended that the IRIDA sample name be the same as, or contain, the specimen collector sample ID for better traceability. It is also recommended that the IRIDA sample name mirror the GISAID accession. IRIDA sample names cannot contain slashes. Slashes should be replaced by underscores. See IRIDA documentation for more information regarding special characters (https://irida.corefacility.ca/documentation/user/user/samples/#adding-a-new-sample).

Slots.name: umbrella_bioproject_accession
Slots.title: umbrella bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number assigned to the umbrella BioProject.
Slots.comments: Store the umbrella BioProject accession by selecting it from the picklist in the template. The umbrella BioProject accession will be identical for all CanCOGen submitters. Different provinces will have their own BioProjects, however these BioProjects will be linked under one umbrella BioProject.

Slots.name: bioproject_accession
Slots.title: bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number of the BioProject(s) to which the BioSample belongs.
Slots.comments: Store the BioProject accession number. BioProjects are an organizing tool that links together raw sequence data, assemblies, and their associated metadata. Each province will be assigned a different bioproject accession number by the National Microbiology Lab. A valid NCBI BioProject accession has prefix PRJN e.g., PRJNA12345, and is created once at the beginning of a new sequencing project.

Slots.name: biosample_accession
Slots.title: biosample accession
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a BioSample in INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the BioSample submission. NCBI BioSamples will have the prefix SAMN.

Slots.name: sra_accession
Slots.title: SRA accession
Slots.description: The Sequence Read Archive (SRA) identifier linking raw read data, methodological metadata and quality control metrics submitted to the INSDC.
Slots.comments: Store the accession assigned to the submitted "run". NCBI-SRA accessions start with SRR.

Slots.name: genbank_accession
Slots.title: GenBank accession
Slots.description: The GenBank identifier assigned to the sequence in the INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from a GenBank submission (viral genome assembly).

Slots.name: gisaid_accession
Slots.title: GISAID accession
Slots.description: The GISAID accession number assigned to the sequence.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the GISAID submission.

Slots.name: gisaid_virus_name
Slots.title: GISAID virus name
Slots.description: The user-defined name of the virus, specified in the organism-specific format prescribed by the GISAID database.
Slots.comments: Provide the GISAID virus name, which should be written in the format: A/Province/Country/SampleID/year

Slots.name: sample_collected_by
Slots.title: sample collected by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that collected the original sample.
Slots.comments: The name of the sample collector should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions e.g. Public Health Agency of Canada, Public Health Ontario, BC Centre for Disease Control. The sample collector specified is at the discretion of the data provider (i.e. may be hospital, provincial public health lab, or other).

Slots.name: sample_collector_contact_email
Slots.title: sample collector contact email
Slots.description: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sample.
Slots.comments: The email address can represent a specific individual or lab e.g. johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca

Slots.name: sequenced_by
Slots.title: sequenced by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that generated the sequence.
Slots.comments: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multiple submissions. If submitting specimens rather than sequencing data, please put the "National Microbiology Laboratory (NML)".

Slots.name: sequence_submitted_by
Slots.title: sequence submitted by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that generated the sequence.
Slots.comments: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions. If submitting specimens rather than sequencing data, please put the "National Microbiology Laboratory (NML)".

Slots.name: sample_collection_date
Slots.title: sample collection date
Slots.description: The date on which the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Sample collection date is critical for surveillance and many types of analyses. Required granularity includes year, month and day. If this date is considered identifiable information, it is acceptable to add "jitter" by adding or subtracting a calendar day (acceptable by GISAID). Alternatively, ”received date” may be used as a substitute. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: sample_collection_date_precision
Slots.title: sample collection date precision
Slots.description: The precision to which the "sample collection date" was provided.
Slots.comments: Provide the precision of granularity to the "day", "month", or "year" for the date provided in the "sample collection date" field. The "sample collection date" will be truncated to the precision specified upon export; "day" for "YYYY-MM-DD", "month" for "YYYY-MM", or "year" for "YYYY".

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_country
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (country)
Slots.description: The country where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the country name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_state_province_territory
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (state/province/territory)
Slots.description: The province/territory where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the province/territory name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: organism
Slots.title: organism
Slots.description: Taxonomic name of the organism.
Slots.comments: Select the type of influenza virus from the picklist provided.

Slots.name: isolate
Slots.title: isolate
Slots.description: Identifier of the specific isolate.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling
Slots.title: purpose of sampling
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: The reason a sample was collected may provide information about potential biases in sampling strategy. Provide the purpose of sampling from the picklist in the template. Most likely, the sample was collected for diagnostic testing. The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing, which should be indicated in the "purpose of sequencing" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling_details
Slots.title: purpose of sampling details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was collected, providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was collected using free text. The description may include the importance of the sample for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. If details are not available, provide a null value.
Slots.examples: The sample was collected to investigate the prevalence of variants associated with mink-to-human transmission in Canada.

Slots.name: nml_submitted_specimen_type
Slots.title: NML submitted specimen type
Slots.description: The type of specimen submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory (NML) for testing.
Slots.comments: This information is required for upload through the CNPHI LaSER system. Select the specimen type from the pick list provided. If sequence data is being submitted rather than a specimen for testing, select “Not Applicable”.

Slots.name: related_specimen_relationship_type
Slots.title: Related specimen relationship type
Slots.description: The relationship of the current specimen to the specimen/sample previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Provide the tag that describes how the previous sample is related to the current sample being submitted from the pick list provided, so that the samples can be linked and tracked in the system.

Slots.name: presampling_activity
Slots.title: presampling_activity
Slots.description: The upstream activities or variables that may affect the sample collected.
Slots.comments: If there was an activity that would affect the sample prior to collection (this is different than sample processing), provide the activities by selecting one or more values from the template pick list. If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Slots.name: presampling_activity_details
Slots.title: presampling activity details
Slots.description: The details of the activities or variables that may affect the sample collected.
Slots.comments: Briefly describe the presampling details using free text.
Slots.examples: Patient was previously infected. Sample taken during convalescence.

Slots.name: anatomical_material
Slots.title: anatomical material
Slots.description: A substance obtained from an anatomical part of an organism e.g. tissue, blood.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical material was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: anatomical_part
Slots.title: anatomical part
Slots.description: An anatomical part of an organism e.g. oropharynx.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical part was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: body_product
Slots.title: body product
Slots.description: A substance excreted/secreted from an organism e.g. feces, urine, sweat.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a body product was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_device
Slots.title: collection device
Slots.description: The instrument or container used to collect the sample e.g. swab.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a device was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_method
Slots.title: collection method
Slots.description: The process used to collect the sample e.g. phlebotomy, necropsy.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a collection method was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_protocol
Slots.title: collection protocol
Slots.description: The name and version of a particular protocol used for sampling.
Slots.comments: Free text.

Slots.name: specimen_processing
Slots.title: specimen processing
Slots.description: Any processing applied to the sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Critical for interpreting data. Select all the applicable processes from the pick list. If virus was passaged, include information in "lab host", "passage number", and "passage method" fields. If none of the processes in the pick list apply, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: specimen_processing_details
Slots.title: specimen processing details
Slots.description: Detailed information regarding the processing applied to a sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of any processing details applied to a sample.
Slots.examples: 25 swabs were pooled and further prepared as a single sample during library prep.

Slots.name: biomaterial_extracted
Slots.title: biomaterial extracted
Slots.description: The biomaterial extracted from samples for the purpose of sequencing.
Slots.comments: Provide the biomaterial extracted from the picklist in the template.

Slots.name: host_common_name
Slots.title: host (common name)
Slots.description: The commonly used name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Common name e.g. human, bat. If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable.

Slots.name: host_scientific_name
Slots.title: host (scientific name)
Slots.description: The taxonomic, or scientific name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Scientific name e.g. Homo sapiens, If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable

Slots.name: host_health_state
Slots.title: host health state
Slots.description: Health status of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_status_details
Slots.title: host health status details
Slots.description: Further details pertaining to the health or disease status of the host at time of collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_outcome
Slots.title: host health outcome
Slots.description: Disease outcome in the host.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_disease
Slots.title: host disease
Slots.description: The name of the disease experienced by the host.
Slots.comments: Select "Influenza" from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_age
Slots.title: host age
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling.
Slots.comments: Enter the age of the host in years. If not available, provide a null value. If there is not host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_age_unit
Slots.title: host age unit
Slots.description: The unit used to measure the host age, in either months or years.
Slots.comments: Indicate whether the host age is in months or years. Age indicated in months will be binned to the 0 - 9 year age bin.

Slots.name: host_age_bin
Slots.title: host age bin
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling, expressed as an age group.
Slots.comments: Select the corresponding host age bin from the pick list provided in the template. If not available, provide a null value.

Slots.name: host_gender
Slots.title: host gender
Slots.description: The gender of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: Select the corresponding host gender from the pick list provided in the template. If not available, provide a null value. If there is no host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_subject_id
Slots.title: host subject ID
Slots.description: A unique identifier by which each host can be referred to e.g. #131
Slots.comments: Provide the host identifier. Should be a unique, user-defined identifier.

Slots.name: host_vaccination_status
Slots.title: host vaccination status
Slots.description: The vaccination status of the host (fully vaccinated, partially vaccinated, or not vaccinated).
Slots.comments: Select the vaccination status of the host from the pick list.

Slots.name: vaccination_history
Slots.title: vaccination history
Slots.description: A description of the vaccines received and the administration dates of a series of vaccinations against a specific disease or a set of diseases.
Slots.comments: Free text description of the dates and vaccines administered against a particular disease/set of diseases. It is also acceptable to concatenate the individual dose information (vaccine name, vaccination date) separated by semicolons.

Slots.name: exposure_event
Slots.title: exposure event
Slots.description: Event leading to exposure.
Slots.comments: Select an exposure event from the pick list provided in the template. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_contact_level
Slots.title: exposure contact level
Slots.description: The exposure transmission contact type.
Slots.comments: Select direct or indirect exposure from the pick-list.

Slots.name: host_role
Slots.title: host role
Slots.description: The role of the host in relation to the exposure setting.
Slots.comments: Select the host's personal role(s) from the pick list provided in the template. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_setting
Slots.title: exposure setting
Slots.description: The setting leading to exposure.
Slots.comments: Select the host exposure setting(s) from the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_details
Slots.title: exposure details
Slots.description: Additional host exposure information.
Slots.comments: Free text description of the exposure.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sequencing
Slots.title: purpose of sequencing
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was sequenced.
Slots.comments: The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing. The reason a sample was sequenced may provide information about potential biases in sequencing strategy. Provide the purpose of sequencing from the picklist in the template. The reason for sample collection should be indicated in the "purpose of sampling" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sequencing_details
Slots.title: purpose of sequencing details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was sequenced providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was sequenced using free text. The description may include the importance of the sequences for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. Suggested standardized descriotions include: Screened for S gene target failure (S dropout), Screened for mink variants, Screened for B.1.1.7 variant, Screened for B.1.135 variant, Screened for P.1 variant, Screened due to travel history, Screened due to close contact with infected individual, Assessing public health control measures, Determining early introductions and spread, Investigating airline-related exposures, Investigating temporary foreign worker, Investigating remote regions, Investigating health care workers, Investigating schools/universities, Investigating reinfection.

Slots.name: sequencing_date
Slots.title: sequencing date
Slots.description: The date the sample was sequenced.
Slots.comments: ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: amplicon_size
Slots.title: amplicon size
Slots.description: The length of the amplicon generated by PCR amplification.
Slots.comments: Provide the amplicon size, including the units.

Slots.name: library_preparation_kit
Slots.title: library preparation kit
Slots.description: The name of the DNA library preparation kit used to generate the library being sequenced.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the library preparation kit used.

Slots.name: sequencing_instrument
Slots.title: sequencing instrument
Slots.description: The model of the sequencing instrument used.
Slots.comments: Select a sequencing instrument from the picklist provided in the template.

Slots.name: sequencing_protocol
Slots.title: sequencing protocol
Slots.description: The protocol used to generate the sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of the methods and materials used to generate the sequence. Suggested text, fill in information where indicated.: "Viral sequencing was performed following a tiling amplicon strategy using the <fill in> primer scheme. Sequencing was performed using a <fill in> sequencing instrument. Libraries were prepared using <fill in> library kit. "
Slots.examples: Genomes were generated through amplicon sequencing of 300 bp amplicons with ARTIC schema primers. Libraries were created using Illumina DNA Prep kits, and sequence data was produced using Miseq Micro v2 (500 cycles) sequencing kits.

Slots.name: amplicon_pcr_primer_scheme
Slots.title: amplicon pcr primer scheme
Slots.description: The specifications of the primers (primer sequences, binding positions, fragment size generated etc) used to generate the amplicons to be sequenced.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version of the primer scheme used to generate the amplicons for sequencing.

Slots.name: raw_sequence_data_processing_method
Slots.title: raw sequence data processing method
Slots.description: The names of the software and version number used for raw data processing such as removing barcodes, adapter trimming, filtering etc.
Slots.comments: Provide the software name followed by the version e.g. Trimmomatic v. 0.38, Porechop v. 0.2.3

Slots.name: dehosting_method
Slots.title: dehosting method
Slots.description: The method used to remove host reads from the pathogen sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version number of the software used to remove host reads.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_software_name
Slots.title: consensus sequence software name
Slots.description: The name of software used to generate the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_software_version
Slots.title: consensus sequence software version
Slots.description: The version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: breadth_of_coverage_value
Slots.title: breadth of coverage value
Slots.description: The percentage of the reference genome covered by the sequenced data, to a prescribed depth.
Slots.comments: Provide value as a percent.

Slots.name: depth_of_coverage_value
Slots.title: depth of coverage value
Slots.description: The average number of reads representing a given nucleotide in the reconstructed sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide value as a fold of coverage.

Slots.name: depth_of_coverage_threshold
Slots.title: depth of coverage threshold
Slots.description: The threshold used as a cut-off for the depth of coverage.
Slots.comments: Provide the threshold fold coverage.

Slots.name: number_of_base_pairs_sequenced
Slots.title: number of base pairs sequenced
Slots.description: The number of total base pairs generated by the sequencing process.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: consensus_genome_length
Slots.title: consensus genome length
Slots.description: Size of the reconstructed genome described as the number of base pairs.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: reference_genome_accession
Slots.title: reference genome accession
Slots.description: A persistent, unique identifier of a genome database entry.
Slots.comments: Provide the accession number of the reference genome.

Slots.name: bioinformatics_protocol
Slots.title: bioinformatics protocol
Slots.description: A description of the overall bioinformatics strategy used.
Slots.comments: Further details regarding the methods used to process raw data, and/or generate assemblies, and/or generate consensus sequences can. This information can be provided in an SOP or protocol or pipeline/workflow. Provide the name and version number of the protocol, or a GitHub link to a pipeline or workflow.

Slots.name: gene_name_1
Slots.title: gene name 1
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of the gene used in the test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_1
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 1
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: gene_name_2
Slots.title: gene name 2
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of another gene used in an RT-PCR test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_2
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 2
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the second diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: gene_name_3
Slots.title: gene name 3
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of another gene used in an RT-PCR test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_3
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 3
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the second diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: authors
Slots.title: authors
Slots.description: Names of individuals contributing to the processes of sample collection, sequence generation, analysis, and data submission.
Slots.comments: Include the first and last names of all individuals that should be attributed, separated by a comma.
Slots.examples: Tejinder Singh, Fei Hu, Joe Blogs

Slots.name: dataharmonizer_provenance
Slots.title: DataHarmonizer provenance
Slots.description: The DataHarmonizer software and template version provenance.
Slots.comments: The current software and template version information will be automatically generated in this field after the user utilizes the "validate" function. This information will be generated regardless as to whether the row is valid of not.

Classes.name: Influenza
Classes.description: Draft template for harmonizing human influenza virus genomic surveillance contextual data.
